patent: CBN Nano Technologies patent, filed 2015-12-31, issued 2019-11-19; inventors Merkle, Freitas, Ryley, Moses and Hogg. It sets out mechanical computers built from very few part types: links and rotary joints (MLL), links and flexures (MFL), or cables, pulleys and knobs (MCL). Locks and balances are the central mechanisms; driven by a multi-phase clock they form logic gates and shift registers, which the text argues is enough for a Turing-complete system. It also sorts mechanical computers into Types 1-4 by how they store and release potential energy. Energy and speed figures are simulation results and estimates for a molecular-scale, diamond-based embodiment (below 1x10E-25 J for a one-radian link rotation at 1x10E9 radians/sec and 180K; switching times of 1 ns to 10 ns). The document describes designs and simulations and reports no built device; it says its figures are didactic sub-assemblies, not complete working mechanisms. Claims 1 and 10 cover lock-and-balance structures. Family, from Google Patents data checked 2026-11-02: continuations US 10,664,233 and US 10,942,704 carry the same drawing captions; continuation-in-part US 10,949,166 adds FIG. 43-55.

glossary.def: Rigid links joined by pivots, so that motion at one point sets motion elsewhere. Here it carries data and also performs logic.
Two parallel support links, a data link across their tops and the anchor block. Used here to constrain a data link to two positions, 0 and 1. The description notes that some call it a 3-bar linkage.

glossary.term: link, data link, support link, line
glossary.def: A link is a rigid body with one or more rotary joints. A data link helps move data; a support link only restrains other links. A line is a chain of connected data links sharing one value.
A connection allowing rotation about an axis. At the molecular scale the patent uses rotation about single bonds; at larger scales, bearings.
An anchored joint is fixed relative to the anchor block. A conditional anchor is fixed only while a lock holds it, which lets the data set which side of a balance moves.
The capsule with an anchored end in many figures. A driver required by the Linkage v3 simulator, standing in for a data line or clock connection; not a part of MLL.
A mechanism where setting one input blocks the others. A two-input binary lock has three states: (0,0) blank, (0,1) and (1,0). From a locked state the only motion allowed is back to blank.
A structure that sends motion down one side or route rather than another. Here usually a link with the input at its center and locks on its ends deciding which end moves.
A balance with locks as conditional anchors, so that control inputs route a third input to one of two outputs.
Two 2-input balances joined by a fixed-length link, which conserves the sum of the inputs.
The patent's encoding for lock-based gates: one line moves for 0 and another for 1, so either value can set a lock. Now commonly called dual-rail encoding.

Here a mechanical clock signal is reciprocating motion on a line or rigid frame. It synchronizes mechanisms and supplies the driving force: inputs are set in one phase, and the clock moves the balances in a later one. Sine-like transitions are preferred to avoid exciting resonances.
Borrowed from relays. Here, no force is applied to a mechanism that is not free to move.

Logic that discards no information, so it is not subject to the Landauer Limit. Here obtained with gates such as Fredkin, by carrying inputs forward with outputs, or by running clock phases in the opposite order.
A minimum of ln(2) kBT dissipated per irreversible bit operation. The description gives 1.72x10E-21 J at 180K.
A universal reversible gate with three inputs and three outputs: A passes through; A = 0 sends B to Y and C to Z; A = 1 swaps them.
Logic stages are set in sequence and later released in reverse order, so results are uncomputed instead of erased. The description notes this may require storing 'junk' bits.
As commonly used in adiabatic logic, a multi-phase scheme in which each stage switches, holds and then releases in turn. The description names a three-phase form.

The sequential element here. Holding-area locks take the input; on the clock phase the data moves to an output lock, which is what stores a previous value. Each cell has three stable states: 0, 1 and blank.

The patent's own classes of mechanical computer. Type 1 releases stored energy unconstrained by the computational degrees of freedom; Type 2 releases it under their control; Type 3 stores only trivial energy but has non-trivial unconstrained degrees of freedom; Type 4 has neither.

Mechanical Linkage Logic (links and rotary joints), Mechanical Flexure Logic (links and flexures), Mechanical Cable Logic (cables, pulleys, knobs). The summary and claims say 'Mechanical Link Logic' for MLL.
A bearing that moves by bending material rather than by sliding or rolling. The description argues it can serve for kinematic restraint alone, with trivial stored energy.

MCL structures. An oval is a closed loop of cable around pulleys; a knob is a block on a cable that interferes with another cable's knobs to form a lock. The description says the knob has no direct MLL or MFL counterpart.
A set of structures moved in opposition so that center of mass and torque do not change and less energy couples into the anchor block.
Standard meaning, with the patent's caveat that real systems have bounded memory and time, making them linear bounded automata. Its definition of a computing system excludes special-purpose devices.
Building structures through positionally controlled chemical reactions. Named here only as one possible way to manufacture molecular-scale parts.
